posts.title: Foreign Direct Investment in Dubai for American Investors: Routes Explained
posts.excerpt: Three ways American investors can hold an investment in Dubai: mainland, free zone and branch, with funding and home-country points.
posts.author: Al Anfal Doc Team
posts.contentHtml:
American investors have three main ways to hold an investment in Dubai: a mainland company, a free zone company, or a branch or representative office of an existing company. Each gives a different legal position, so choose by activity, customers and how much control you need.

The three routes at a glance

  • Mainland company - licensed by the Department of Economy and Tourism, can trade across the UAE, and most activities allow 100% foreign ownership.
  • Free zone company - licensed by the zone, good for services and trading with clients abroad; trading directly with mainland customers has extra rules.
  • Branch or representative office - lets a company from the United States operate under its own name; the parent stays legally responsible.

What suits American investors

American founders and remote teams use Dubai as a base for clients in the Middle East, South Asia and Africa, and some move operations to work in a time zone that overlaps with Asia and Europe. Because the dirham is pegged to the dollar, contracts and budgets in dollars are easy to plan. Investors from California and other parts of the United States often start with a small operating company, and add structure later. Sectors tied to the United States include technology, entertainment, agriculture and trade through the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach.

Funding and home-country rules

Transfers from US banks to a Dubai company account are usually wires. Banks on both sides ask about the source of funds and the purpose, so keep invoices, agreements and share-capital papers ready. US citizens and residents are generally taxed on worldwide income wherever they live, and owners of foreign companies can have reporting duties such as FATCA-related forms, FBAR filings for foreign accounts and information returns for controlled foreign corporations. There is no comprehensive US-UAE income tax treaty, so confirm your position with a US tax adviser before you form the company.

Where we fit

We prepare licence applications, documents and approvals; see company formation and government approvals and clearances. The full route is in our United States of America country guide, and our mainland versus free zone guide explains the choice.

Questions American owners ask

How long does it take?

Timing depends on the activity, approvals and how fast documents from the United States are legalised. Plan in weeks rather than days and ask for a written timeline.

Can I invest remotely?

Often the paperwork can be done from the United States with a power of attorney, but residence visa steps need a visit. Dubai is 12 hours ahead of California in winter and 11 hours ahead in summer, so calls are usually held in the California evening or the Dubai morning.

What should I check at home?

Reporting, tax and foreign-exchange rules in the United States. The IRS (irs.gov) and your own tax adviser can advise.

posts.title: Holding Company in the UAE for British Owners: Structuring Responsibly
posts.excerpt: How British owners can use a UAE holding company: purpose, substance, corporate tax and the documents involved.
posts.author: Al Anfal Doc Team
posts.contentHtml:
A holding company owns shares in other businesses. British owners use UAE holdings to bring several companies, investments or assets under one owner, and to simplify succession and banking. It must be genuine: real decisions, proper records and honest filings.

Why owners consider a holding

  • One owner for several operating companies, with clear shareholding records.
  • A single point for dividends and reinvestment decisions.
  • Easier discussion with banks and partners.

Substance and tax come first

Corporate tax is 9% above AED 375,000 of taxable income, and conditions apply to relief for qualifying holdings. See the Federal Tax Authority for the current rules. UK tax residence is decided under the Statutory Residence Test, and UK residents can be taxed on worldwide income. Controlled foreign company rules and the UK-UAE double tax agreement may apply to a Dubai company, so speak to a UK tax adviser before deciding where directors live and where decisions are taken.

A holding set up only to avoid tax at home can fail and can carry penalties. Our team does not advise on avoiding tax; we prepare the legal and licensing documents once your advisers have settled the structure.

What we prepare

Memorandum of association drafting, licence, shareholder documents and attestation of home papers. See MOA drafting and amendments, company formation and the United Kingdom country guide. Home documents follow this route: UK documents are normally notarised or certified and then legalised with an apostille issued through the UK government's legalisation service, followed by any extra UAE step that applies. Certified originals are needed, so do not rely on scans.

Questions British owners ask

Does a holding company save tax?

It can change where profit is taxed, but substance, records and home-country rules decide the result. Treat any promise of zero tax with caution.

What records are needed?

Shareholder registers, board minutes, accounts and evidence that decisions are taken where you say. Banks in the United Kingdom and Dubai may ask for them.

Can we add subsidiaries later?

Yes. A clear shareholding structure at the start makes later additions simpler.

posts.title: Ejari Rules for Chinese Business Owners: Register Your Dubai Lease
posts.excerpt: What Ejari is, which documents are needed and common mistakes for Chinese business owners registering a Dubai lease.
posts.author: Al Anfal Doc Team
posts.contentHtml:
Ejari is the Dubai registration system for tenancy contracts, run by the Dubai Land Department. A mainland trade licence normally needs a registered lease, so Chinese owners meet Ejari early.

What Ejari does

  • Records the lease between landlord and tenant officially.
  • Gives the licence authority proof of premises.
  • Protects both sides if there is a dispute.

Typical documents

Usually the signed tenancy contract, the landlord's ownership proof, and the tenant's passport and licence details. A company from China may also need its own papers; Documents issued in Shanghai go through the apostille or consular route that applies to the document, handled by the competent Chinese authority, and normally need a certified translation.

Common mistakes

  • Signing a lease before checking it suits the licence activity.
  • Names on the lease that differ from the licence.
  • Letting the registration lapse at renewal.

Options for small teams

Some businesses use a flexible desk. See virtual office and Ejari registration and our trade licence service. Chinese owners paying rent from China can read about transfers in the China country guide.

Questions Chinese owners ask

Is Ejari needed for a free zone?

Free zones usually provide their own lease or flexi-desk, so the rules differ from the mainland. Ask the zone.

What if the landlord will not register?

A lease that cannot be registered usually cannot support a mainland licence. Choose another property.

Who pays the registration fee?

Omani investors have three main ways to hold an investment in Dubai: a mainland company, a free zone company, or a branch or representative office of an existing company. Each gives a different legal position, so choose by activity, customers and how much control you need.

The three routes at a glance

Omani businesses and investors use Dubai for trading, logistics, services and investment holdings, helped by the short distance and the shared regional market. Many owners keep an Omani base and add a Dubai licence for UAE customers. Investors from Muscat Governorate and other parts of Oman often start with a small operating company, and add structure later. Sectors tied to Oman include government, trade, logistics and tourism, with a main port at Muttrah.

Transfers between Omani and UAE banks are international payments. Banks ask for the purpose and the source of funds, so keep invoices, agreements and capital documents ready.
